$comment: Raw Polona responses captured by TASK-031 (docs/sources/polona.md). Every committed byte is what Polona served. The only change is to two full-text search responses, from which whole hits were removed by byte-level excision (see trimming). Nothing else was trimmed, reformatted or re-encoded. `fixtures/polona/` is excluded from Prettier for that reason. Verify with: cd fixtures/polona && sha256sum -c <(jq -r '.files[] | "\(.sha256)  \(.path)"' source-manifest.json)

capture.pacing: one request at a time; 1.5 s between search requests, 1.2 s between object requests
capture.authentication: none (no cookie, token or key sent)

query_set.chosen_as: rare surname with a diacritic, from fixtures/pesel/regional-male-2026-01-20.csv
surname that is also an ordinary Polish word (wolf)

trimming.rule: A full-text hit carries OCR snippets (`highlights`). A full-text hit is kept only when its attributes.licenseName is "Domena Publiczna", Polona's own public-domain statement. Every other full-text hit was removed whole. Metadata-search hits carry no OCR text and were all kept.
trimming.method: Byte-level excision of the hit's exact span and one separating comma. Every other byte, including numberOfElements, is as served, so a trimmed file has fewer hits than its numberOfElements says. Its as_served.sha256 is the digest of the untrimmed response.
trimming.ocr_text_sha256_definition: SHA-256 of the UTF-8 encoding of the hit's `highlights` strings, as JSON-decoded, joined with a single "\n"
trimming.hit_bytes_sha256_definition: SHA-256 of the hit's exact bytes as served, without the separating comma
